text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Bank employees' unions are challenging a secret agreement between leading bank data-processing companies to reject job-seekers from each other's firms.
--The state comptroller's office is investigating the award by the social affairs ministry of projects to set up nursing homes in Poland to a company on whose board sit ministry officials.

--The continuing rise in share prices has forced pension fund LD to sell 500 million crowns worth of stock this year and buy bonds, in order to comply with rules limiting its share investments to 35 percent of its total funds. It is likely to sell another 700 million crowns this autumn.
--Pork producers are hard hit by swine diseases, with one in four animals affected.
--Farmers are getting a record harvest this year, with corn production alone worth about 9.8 billion crowns and expected to have a positive effect on the balance of trade. REUTER SCW
